name: Mireille & The Hollow Saints
description:
Mireille Oduya-Chekhov is a Shelf-born vocalist and neural composer who, between 2209 and 2217, released seven albums under the name Mireille & The Hollow Saints — the 'Saints' being a rotating cast of session musicians, most of them anonymous to avoid corporate retaliation. Her music is built on a foundation of Eastern Orthodox choral tradition, Igbo ceremonial music, and a highly unconventional use of BCI composition: Mireille composes directly from neural state, recording raw cognitive and emotional architecture and translating it into harmonic structure through a custom-built interface she calls 'the Confessional.' The resulting music is, by all accounts, deeply uncomfortable to listen to — not unpleasant, but nakedly intimate, as if the listener is overhearing something they were never meant to.

In 2217, her seventh album 'Ledger of the Unnamed' was pulled from all licensed feeds within seventy-two hours of release. The official reason given was 'harmonic content exceeding neural safety parameters.' Researchers and fans who analyzed the pulled tracks found no such content. The album had included, embedded in the liner metadata, a full documented account of a Vantablack Media subsidiary's use of acoustic and neural-feed technology to suppress a Circuit-tier labor action in 2215. Mireille has not released music publicly since. Her current location is unknown. The album circulates on encrypted pirate mesh and is considered one of the most important banned recordings in Meridian 88's history.
creator: Mireille Oduya-Chekhov
genre: Neural Confessional, Sacred Drone, BCI-Composed Choral
audience: Underground music communities across all tiers, anti-Vantablack activists, journalists, anyone who has managed to obtain the pirate feed
cultural_impact: The disappearance of 'Ledger of the Unnamed' and the subsequent silence of Mireille Oduya-Chekhov have made her one of the most discussed absent figures in Meridian 88's cultural landscape. The question of whether she is in hiding, detained, or dead is asked openly in underground circles and carefully avoided in licensed media. The album itself has taken on a documentary significance beyond its music — the embedded labor suppression data has been cited in at least two underground journalist investigations. That the music is also genuinely extraordinary compounds its mythic status. Mireille & The Hollow Saints are, for many listeners across tiers, proof that the censorship apparatus is working — and that something worth suppressing existed.
known_fans: Tier 3 and 4 listeners who obtained pirate copies
story_hooks: A contact slips the party a data chip containing what they claim is an unreleased eighth album — recorded after Mireille's disappearance. The audio is unmistakably hers. The metadata contains something that looks like a location.

A Vantablack corporate security officer is quietly, off-the-record, trying to find out what happened to Mireille Oduya-Chekhov — not to finish the job, but because something about the official story doesn't add up and it's keeping him up at night.

The party is hired to transport a physical drive containing the complete master recordings of 'Ledger of the Unnamed' from one safehouse to another — three different factions, including a Vantablack retrieval team, already know the transfer is happening.
